slides.title: Welcome to the Children's Constitution Club!
slides.subtitle: Diversity & Composite Culture - 2
slides.tip: Play welcome music. Confirm everyone is seated in groups.

slides.title: Cherishing Our Diversity
slides.transcript: Hello everyone! Today I have a question to ask you all. Before that I would like all of you to close your eyes. Don't answer aloud and don't share. My question is: When I say the words "Our culture", what pictures come to your mind? Think about it for 20 seconds.
kn_script: ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ! ಇಂದು ನಾನು ನಿಮಗೆಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಒಂದು ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕೇಳಬೇಕು. ಅದಕ್ಕೂ ಮೊದಲು ನೀವೆಲ್ಲರೂ ಕಣ್ಣು ಮುಚ್ಚಿ.
ನನ್ನ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಇದು: ನಾನು "ನಮ್ಮ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ" ಎಂಬ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ಹೇಳಿದಾಗ, ನಿಮ್ಮ ಮನಸ್ಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವ ಚಿತ್ರಗಳು ಬರುತ್ತವೆ?
slides.tip: Play the MC video. After the video, give students 20 seconds of silence to think. Then ask 2-3 children to share what images came to mind.

slides.title: Composite Culture Picture Activity
slides.brief: Look at the Composite Culture picture sheet distributed to your group. Pick 3 pictures that you think best describe Our Culture and write down in your notebook why you chose them.
slides.tip: Distribute Composite Culture picture sheet (1 per group). Start the 4-minute timer. Walk around and encourage discussion.

slides.title: Discuss — India's Diversity
body: What are some Indian states you know? What makes them unique?
How does this diversity contribute to our culture? Discuss!
slides.tip: Kerala is known for Kathakali, Rajasthan for forts and folk music, Odisha for Pattachitra paintings, Punjab for Bhangra and cuisine. Get responses from 3-4 groups.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi Game!
body: We will now have a fun game!
You will see pictures of different daily items/food products and you have to guess if it's:
DESI — invented in or originally from India
or VIDESI — from a country other than India!
Ready?
slides.tip: Build excitement! Explain the rules clearly before starting.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Tea

items.label: TEA — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from China! Tea was brought to India by the British in the 19th century.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Pepper

items.label: PEPPER — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: DESI! It's from India! India has been called the 'Land of Spices' and pepper is native to Kerala.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Tomato

items.label: TOMATO — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from Mexico! Tomatoes were brought to India by the Portuguese.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Paper

items.label: PAPER — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from China! Paper was invented in China around 100 BC.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Potato

items.label: POTATO — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from Peru! Potatoes came to India through Portuguese traders.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Carrot

items.label: CARROT — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from Persia! Carrots spread to India through Persian trade routes.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Desi-Videsi: Coffee

items.label: COFFEE — Desi or Videsi?
items.detail: VIDESI! It's from Ethiopia! Coffee was brought to India by Baba Budan from Yemen in the 17th century.

slides.tip: Let groups shout out their guess. Click to reveal the answer.

slides.title: Discuss the Desi-Videsi Results
slides.prompt: Let's reflect on what we just discovered!
body: How do you feel about what we just found out?
These give you an important clue about India's culture. Can you guess what it is?
slides.tip: Guide students toward realizing that many everyday items came from outside India — our culture borrows and adapts from many places.

slides.title: Composite Culture
body: Our culture is known as a 'Composite Culture'.
What is 'Composite'?
Our Composite Culture is diverse, different and mixed; and has come from the many parts of India and outside India.
slides.tip: Explain: 'Composite' means made of many parts. Our culture is a mix of Indian and foreign influences that we have adopted and made our own.

slides.title: Composite Culture — Examples
body: Tomatoes — from Mexico, brought to India by the Portuguese!
Cricket — brought to India by the British who ruled over us for many years!
Are tomatoes and cricket part of our culture? Absolutely! We adopted them and made them uniquely ours.

images.caption: From Mexico, brought by the Portuguese!

slides.tip: Emphasize: we borrow things from other cultures and make them our own — that's what composite culture means.

slides.title: Composite Culture — Fundamental Duty
body: We lend and borrow, adapt and change to make it something unique.
This is a Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution.
Can anyone guess what that Fundamental Duty says?
We must respect and preserve the rich cultural heritage of the country, which is a composite of various cultures, religions and traditions.
slides.callout: Fundamental Duty: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
slides.tip: Ask students to guess before revealing. This is Article 51A(f) of the Indian Constitution.

slides.title: Reflection
slides.transcript: Can we accept people, practices and different ways of life the same way? What do you feel? Have you accepted all your classmates even though they are different from you in habits, customs, practices?
kn_script: ನಾವು ಜನರನ್ನು, ಆಚರಣೆಗಳನ್ನು ಮತ್ತು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ಜೀವನ ವಿಧಾನಗಳನ್ನು ಅದೇ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸಬಹುದೇ?
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಹಪಾಠಿಗಳು ಅಭ್ಯಾಸಗಳು, ಪದ್ಧತಿಗಳು, ಆಚರಣೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಮ್ಮಿಂದ ಭಿನ್ನರಾಗಿದ್ದರೂ ನೀವು ಅವರೆಲ್ಲರನ್ನೂ ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸಿದ್ದೀರಾ?
slides.tip: Play the MC video. Let children think and share. This is a moment for honest self-reflection — don't rush it.

slides.title: Preamble Cards — Constitution Connection
body: Which Constitutional value best connects to you today as part of the activities and discussions we have had?
slides.tip: Show the preamble value cards. Ask each group to pick the value that resonated most with today's session and explain why.

slides.title: Reflection Circle
slides.prompt: Form a 'Reflection Circle' in your groups by putting your hands on top of each other.
body: What kind of beliefs and ideas did you come to this session with?
How has your thinking or belief system changed after the session?
What surprised you in the session and made you change your stand?
slides.tip: Each group forms a circle with hands stacked. Go around the circle — each child answers one question. Ensure every child gets a turn.

slides.title: Ripple Task
body: Conduct a Desi-Videsi quiz for your parents and siblings!
Look at everyday items and think about how they contribute to composite culture!
slides.callout: Take the quiz home! Test your family on what's Desi and what's Videsi.
slides.tip: Encourage students to quiz at least 3 family members and report back next session.

slides.title: Constitution Connect — Quiz
slides.question: Which Fundamental Duty emphasizes the importance of preserving India's diverse cultural heritage?
options: Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
slides.tip: Let groups discuss for 30 seconds before answering. The correct answer is (a) — Article 51A(e) promotes harmony and brotherhood among all people of India.

slides.title: Together for Change Project
body: You have 3 weeks to complete the activities given in the project card.
Please follow the instructions provided in the project cards thoroughly in your groups.
Consult the teacher if you have doubts!
slides.callout: Distribute Together for Change cards on Diversity and Composite Culture to each group.
slides.tip: Distribute Together for Change project cards. Explain the 3-week timeline. Each group works together on their project.
